Subject: Urgent - sudden throughput cliff + nonsensical responses since last night

Hi Priyom / Monica,

We started seeing a large regression right after the model swap you rolled last night (v4alpha + int8 qprofile). High-level: throughput is down ~45% for our hotpath, p99 latency roughly doubled, and ~4.8% 5xx error rate on completion calls. Equally worrying — our QA team pulled a sample of responses and flagged a jump in incoherent outputs (replies that contradict user context, fabricated references).

I attached a small sample set (sample-responses.json) and we have a few request traces that show long-tailed token decoding. We urgently need a remediation plan. Can you confirm whether this is a config/quant profile issue and whether rollback is possible? This is impacting customer flows and our payments reconciliation.

Alex
Head of Integrations, HeliosCard

Alex — thanks for the quick heads up and the sample data. I pulled the first set and shared with infra/eng. Short answers up front: we see the same signal and are treating this as P1.

Immediate asks so we can triage faster:
- Can you confirm (by PM or SRE) which endpoint & route is the hotpath (example route id or example request id from the traces)?
- If you have peak qps windows/times, send them (we want to correlate with batch sizing & autoscale).
- Please keep traffic to the hotpath throttled to <50% for the next 2 hours if you can (to reduce error amplification).

We are evaluating two immediate mitigations:
1) Rollback to previous model/quant profile (v4beta + qprofile-v2) — requires a signed exec approval from our side and ~45m downtime on that route for a controlled flip.
2) Hotpatch: temporarily disable the int8 decode path and force float fallback + reduced batch sizes — lower impact but may increase cost.

I'll loop in eng (karthik) and CS (Monica) to coordinate. We'll follow up within 30 minutes with a recommended plan.

— Priyom

Thanks for the alert and the artifacts — we reproduced the signal in our test harness. Quick diagnostic summary:
- Root hypothesis: the int8 quant profile for v4alpha introduced token-by-token probability skew on longer sequences. That skew increases the expected output length in a small subset of prompts, which causes KV cache miss amplification and backpressure in the continuous-batching layer.
- Observable consequences: p99 decode time increases significantly for affected requests, batches that used to fit become oversized --> memory churn --> partial fallbacks and 5xx completions. The incoherent outputs appear tied to probability mass reshaping from quant noise; in a few cases the sampling distribution drifts away from the fine-tuned logits.

What we recommend (ordered by risk):
A) Emergency rollback: flip HeliosCard hot route back to v4beta + qprofile-v2. This is the cleanest fix for both latency and coherence. Estimated disruption: 45 minutes of controlled flip, coordinated cache flush, and one warmup window.
B) Hotpatch (if rollback needs approval): disable int8 decode path for HeliosCard and force float fallback, reduce max batch size from 32 -> 8 and enable KV prefix sticky caching for hot keys. This will increase cost (estimated +18% token cost) but reduces p99.
C) Medium term: re-run quantization with longer tail calibration and add a token-level QA eval set specific to HeliosCard flows (we'll maintain this in RW evals).

We've attached profiling-summary.csv with per-shard decode times and an initial regression run. If you want to move forward with A) I need an exec approval to initiate the flip and a rails ticket (we'll open RW-5921).

Karthik
Principal Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
